correctness.rationale: The homogenous degree-ten equations vanish at all 57 F_7 points. The Asgarli--Ghioca rational-singularity criterion and direct substitution leave k=1,3. Exact Buchberger reductions of all three gradient polynomials to the unit ideal in all three affine charts independently prove geometric smoothness for both. For the 36 adjoint monomials of degree 7, the classical plane-curve Hasse--Witt coefficient formula gives 36x36 matrices computed from F_k^6 over F_7. Exact Gaussian elimination finds rank(A)=rank(A^2)=35; 35x35 minors have determinants 6,1 (k=1) and 6,6 (k=3) while both full determinants vanish. Therefore a=1, stable rank/p-rank=35 and the Newton polygon is 0^35, (1/2)^2, 1^35. Exhaustive F_49 counts in two independent quadratic field presentations produce 103 and 107, respectively. Each computation is replayed from the actual attached scripts.

originality.rationale: The initiating 2023 paper defines this precise pencil and establishes its rational singularity criterion, general smoothness computations, and plane-filling property. The new claim is about the complete arithmetic classification of its two smooth F_7 members: their almost-ordinary Hasse--Witt matrices, 7-ranks, a-numbers, Newton slopes, and distinct quadratic-extension point counts. The full accessible 2023 paper contains no corresponding p-rank, a-number, Hasse--Witt rank, Newton polygon, or F_49 count claim. Adolphson--Sperber provides the general formula, not its computation for this pencil. Targeted published-database searches returned no equivalent; this is best-knowledge originality, not a proof of worldwide priority.
residual_risks: An unindexed or unpublished p-rank computation for the same pencil may exist.
The general literature on arithmetic of plane-filling curves is not guaranteed exhaustively searchable; no universal priority proof is claimed.

value.rationale: The Asgarli--Ghioca degree-q+3 pencil is a canonical explicit source of smooth plane-filling curves. At q=7 its two smooth members are natural exhaustive arithmetic test cases in genus 36, not an arbitrary coefficient slice: the field characteristic coincides with the exponent seven in the original singularity test. The result fixes the exact p-divisible slopes and Cartier defect for every smooth member and separates their isogeny classes via a natural extension-field count. Near-maximal p-rank despite passing through all 57 rational plane points is a nontrivial arithmetic phenomenon; the classification can serve as a concrete benchmark for arithmetic studies of high-genus plane-filling curves. It does not claim a uniform-in-q theorem.
